summary: Iter165 — tested the new Super Admin 'Transcription Usage' report (m034 migration + GET /super-admin/transcription-usage-report + SuperAdminTranscriptionUsage.js). Migration verified applied in DB (transcripts.speech_model_used/latency_ms + meetings.failed_stage all exist). Backend pytest suite (14/14 pass, /app/backend/tests/test_transcription_usage_report.py): RBAC (super_admin 200, admin 403, unauth 401), response shape (items + stats keys), seeded row (meeting 2f1cc088... shows speech_model_used=universal-3-5-pro + latency_ms>0), legacy rows correctly return null speech_model_used/latency_ms without crashing, filters (speech_model narrows to exactly that model, unknown model → empty, failed_only → only failed rows, org_id narrows to that org, bogus org → empty, from_date=future → empty, to_date=2000 → empty), stats math self-consistent (total==len(items), by_speech_model sum ≤ total, failure_rate_pct derivable). Frontend Playwright (login as super_admin via cookie injection to bypass MFA UI): 'Transcription Usage' tab visible with data-testid='tab-transcription-usage', all 5 stat cards render (Total=23, Failure Rate=0%, Avg Latency=17.9s, Avg Audio Length=2min with '1 with safety warnings', By Speech Model showing universal-3-5-pro:1), 23 rows in table incl. seeded meeting row with 'universal-3-5-pro' badge + OK status, failed_only checkbox narrows to 0 rows (no failures live), speech_model dropdown narrows to 1 row (seeded meeting), org filter dropdown populated with 11 options, Refresh button clickable, meeting-link opens /meetings/.../report in target='_blank'. Retranscribe API-driven flow already verified by main agent (evidence: seeded meeting 2f1cc088 has real universal-3-5-pro / 17906ms values in DB and surfaces correctly in the report). Full first-scan pipeline INSERT with the 2 new columns was code-reviewed (utils/transcription_pipeline.py L217-223) — INSERT column list matches the 7-tuple unpack at L201, no crash risk. failed_stage attribution on real AssemblyAI failure was code-reviewed (L204-208): meetings.failed_stage='transcription' is UPDATE-d BEFORE the `raise`, so the outer except at L496-503 that sets status='processing_failed'+processing_error runs afterwards on the same row — the report's failed_only filter and red 'Failed' badge WILL pick it up correctly.
action_items: OPTIONAL (minor gap): In routers/processing.py::_run_retranscribe_background (L336-340), when AssemblyAI fails on a re-scan, only meetings.diarize_status='failed' is set — meetings.failed_stage='transcription' is NOT set (and no processing_error is written). Result: a re-scan that fails at AssemblyAI will NOT surface in the Transcription Usage report's 'Failed only' filter or as a red 'Failed' status badge (the first-scan pipeline in transcription_pipeline.py L207 DOES set failed_stage='transcription' correctly). Consider adding `UPDATE meetings SET failed_stage='transcription', processing_error=<err> WHERE id=$1` alongside the diarize_status=failed update in the AssemblyAI except at L336-340 (and possibly also the get_audio failure at L321-323 and the diarization-empty case at L353-356 depending on desired attribution). Not blocking — original first-scan attribution is intact.
critical_code_review_comments: utils/transcription_pipeline.py L207 correctly sets meetings.failed_stage='transcription' BEFORE re-raising the AssemblyAI exception, and the outer except handler at L496-503 then sets status='processing_failed'+processing_error on the same row — so the report's failed_only filter + red status badge will pick up a real first-scan AssemblyAI failure. Verified by tracing the code paths; could not force a live failure since ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY is set and working in this env.

routers/processing.py::_run_retranscribe_background does NOT set meetings.failed_stage on any of its failure paths (audio-load fail, AssemblyAI fail, diarization empty). This means a failing RE-SCAN won't be attributed to the transcription stage in the report — only failing FIRST-SCANS will. See action_items above.

The Transcription Usage endpoint at super_admin.py L722 correctly includes both `t.id IS NOT NULL` AND `m.failed_stage='transcription'` rows, so meetings that failed before creating a transcript row DO appear in the report (this is only reachable via first-scan pipeline today; see prior comment).

SuperAdminTranscriptionUsage.js's ModelBadge classifies as 'primary' (indigo) when the model name contains '3' OR 'pro' — works for universal-3-5-pro (both), and universal-2 would fall back to amber. Slightly brittle if AssemblyAI ever ships e.g. 'universal-2-pro' — that would incorrectly get the indigo/primary badge — but harmless UX cosmetic.

The endpoint LIMITs items to 200 with no pagination; fine for now but as adoption grows this endpoint will need offset+limit or cursor pagination. Same caveat applies to /ai-usage-report and /ai-accuracy-report — pre-existing pattern, not new to this feature.
